questions.stem: Why is carbon monoxide particularly dangerous to humans?

options.text: It has a strong smell that causes headaches
It binds to haemoglobin in the blood, preventing oxygen transport, and is colourless and odourless
It reacts with water in the lungs to form acid
It causes the ozone layer to thin

questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide (CO) is toxic because it binds to haemoglobin more strongly than oxygen, preventing red blood cells from carrying oxygen to body tissues. It is particularly dangerous because it is colourless and odourless, making it very difficult to detect without a detector.
